text:
leah: quick FYI — onboarding call hit an auth surprise: examples/quickstart inferred org from git remote and that inference got persisted to the session, which overrode an explicit REDWOOD_ORG env later. repro: `export REDWOOD_ORG=orgA && git remote set-url origin git@github.com:orgB/repo.git && redwood start` -> requests ended up billed to orgB.

sam: yikes. users expect explicit env vars/flags to be authoritative. inference must be opt-in and never written as authoritative without consent.

mike: proposal for canonical precedence: CLI flag > explicit SDK param > REDWOOD_* env > user-accepted inferred metadata > session cache > system store. Make inferred data require `--accept-inferred-org` or similar.

leah: rotation angle: long-lived processes (workers) keep creds in memory and miss rotations. suggest: 1) export `client.reload_credentials()` in all SDKs; 2) add a tiny SIGHUP handler example in samples; 3) add a `redwood auth preview-session` CLI command to show what would be written without persisting.

auth-bot: created RW-9001 "auth-inferred-metadata-overrides-env" (assignee: sam)

sam: action items I’ll pick up: doc shortform describing precedence, add `preview-session`, add SIGHUP reload example to examples/worker, and a 1-day spike to prototype `--watch-auth` CLI flag that reloads on env change. also add telemetry events `auth.infer_conflict` and `auth.rotation_miss`.

mike: sample worker snippet we can add to repo (python):
```python
import signal
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
def reload(_signum, _frame):
    client.reload_credentials()
signal.signal(signal.SIGHUP, reload)
# long-lived loop here
```

leah: docs note for quickstart: "If we suggest an org from git remote, you must opt in to persist it. To avoid surprises set REDWOOD_ORG explicitly or run `redwood auth preview-session` before accepting." :warning:

sam: will open a PR and tag @leah for review. tagging @eng-devex @platform for parity across SDKs. thanks all :thumbsup:
